sentences.text: A cairn site's public side is a set of routes in the site's SvelteKit app.
The entry pages and their raw-markdown twins, the archive, the RSS and JSON feeds, the sitemap, and `robots.txt` are each a few lines around a function the engine exports.
The app builds with `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare` into the site's one Worker.
The routes prerender: at build time they read the markdown in the commit being deployed and write each page and file, and no public request reads the GitHub repository.
Every route reads the same two inputs: one typed index of the content, built by `createSiteIndexes`, and one origin literal.
Because the build runs the routes, the origin is written into every canonical URL, feed, and sitemap row, and it has to name the deployed origin before a production build.
A scaffolded site already has every route this page covers except a tag page.
Its developer arrives to learn what each route does and where to change it, starting with the origin, which the scaffold ships as a placeholder.

A site built through [Add cairn to a SvelteKit app](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md) has the index and the entry route from that tutorial's [Render the entry](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#render-the-entry) step, and it gains the rest here.

You build the index and the origin, compose one `PublicRoutesConfig`, and wire the entry pages and their twins, the feeds, the sitemap, `robots.txt`, the archive, a tag page, and the public menu behind the admin's `nav` screen, then read the prerendered files after a build.

Two engine limits apply to every site: the engine builds a head only for entry pages, and it takes the hero and the share image only from a frontmatter field named `image`, whatever image field a concept marks for SEO.

[Give other pages a head](#give-other-pages-a-head) and [Declare the fields the head reads](#declare-the-fields-the-head-reads) cover those limits, and [Diagnose a failed build](#diagnose-a-failed-build) covers a build that stops on content.
This page assumes you know SvelteKit routing, including rest parameters, param matchers, route groups, server endpoints, and layout loads, along with its prerendering exports and Vite's glob imports.
Beyond the adapter that declares your site's concepts, it assumes no cairn knowledge.
It leaves out the following topics, each with the page that covers it:
A stance toward AI training crawlers: [Choose an AI posture](choose-an-ai-posture.md).
The draft preview route: [Share a draft preview](share-a-draft-preview.md).
Announcing newly published entries, as opposed to the feeds that subscribers pull: [Act on newly published entries](act-on-newly-published-entries.md).
Resolving `media:` images: [Resolve media on public pages](configure-media.md#resolve-media-on-public-pages).
Styling the pages: [Theme your public site](theme-your-public-site.md).
Arranging the admin's sidebar, which shares the word "nav": [Arrange the admin sidebar](arrange-the-admin-sidebar.md).
The public routes read your adapter and your parsed site config, and they prerender on a SvelteKit site built with `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare`.
Before you start, your site needs the following:
An adapter that declares the site's concepts, at `src/theme/cairn.config.ts` on a scaffolded site and at `src/lib/cairn.config.ts` on the add-cairn tutorial's site.
[Define an adapter and schema](define-an-adapter-and-schema.md) covers it.
A site config, parsed as the [site config reference](../reference/core.md#parsesiteconfig) describes.
A SvelteKit site on `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare`.
A scaffolded site has one, and [Deploy a bare SvelteKit site](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#deploy-a-bare-sveltekit-site) sets one up from scratch.
Optionally, for hero images, a media resolver, which [Resolve media on public pages](configure-media.md#resolve-media-on-public-pages) sets up.
With those in place, start from a map of the files.
Every public route is a file under `src/routes/`, and on a scaffolded site the modules they share sit in `src/chassis/`.
The scaffold's public files are as follows:
Each file belongs to one section of this page:
`src/chassis/content.ts` builds the index and holds the origin, as [Build one typed index](#build-one-typed-index) and [Name the origin once](#name-the-origin-once) show.
`src/chassis/public-routes.ts` holds the shared `PublicRoutesConfig` that [Wire the entry pages](#wire-the-entry-pages) composes.
`(site)/[...path]` is the entry catch-all, also in [Wire the entry pages](#wire-the-entry-pages).
`(site)/[...path=md]` and `src/params.ts` serve the twin in [Serve the markdown twin](#serve-the-markdown-twin).
`feed.xml/`, `feed.json/`, and `src/chassis/feed.ts` serve the feeds in [Serve the feeds](#serve-the-feeds).
`sitemap.xml/` serves the sitemap in [Serve the sitemap](#serve-the-sitemap).
`robots.txt/` serves the crawl rules in [Serve robots.txt](#serve-robotstxt).
`(site)/archive/[page]/` serves the archive in [Build the archive](#build-the-archive).
`(site)/+page.svelte` is the home page, which [Give other pages a head](#give-other-pages-a-head) covers.
The root `src/routes/+layout.server.ts` returns the menu in [Add an editable menu](#add-an-editable-menu).
The tree leaves out the admin's routes and the scaffold's other public routes.
The `preview/[token]/` route under `(site)/` serves draft previews, which [Share a draft preview](share-a-draft-preview.md) covers.
[Routes and the server hook](scaffolded-site-files.md#routes-and-the-server-hook) lists every scaffold route, the admin's included.
On the add-cairn tutorial's site, the same modules and routes sit where that tutorial put them.

[Index the content and commit its manifest](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#index-the-content-and-commit-its-manifest) writes the content module, and [Render the entry](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#render-the-entry) writes the entry route.
Where a section names a scaffold path, use the matching file in your tree.
Start with the content module.
`createSiteIndexes` builds one typed index per concept from one literal `import.meta.glob` per concept, and every public route reads through it.
Vite needs each glob pattern written literally at the call site, so the globs can't be generated in a loop over the concept list.
To build the index, make one call:
In the content module (`src/chassis/content.ts` on a scaffolded site), pass `createSiteIndexes` the adapter, the site config, and one raw, eager glob per concept.
The scaffold's content module makes the call with one glob for each of its three concepts:
The result holds one index per concept, keyed by concept id, plus `site`, the cross-concept resolver.
Because `site` is reserved, no concept can be named `site`.
A lazy glob, or one without `query: '?raw'` and `import: 'default'`, fails the build with the message that [Diagnose a failed build](#diagnose-a-failed-build) lists.
The site config doesn't change the indexes, and `createSiteIndexes` takes it anyway, so pass the parsed config.
Each index's `all()` already returns entries in the engine's order, which [Build the archive](#build-the-archive) relies on.
`all()` and `byTag()` leave out an entry marked `draft: true` unless called with `{ includeDrafts: true }`, and `allTags()` and `adjacent()` always leave it out.
Because the resolver builds its permalink lookup from `all()`, a draft never resolves or prerenders.
`byId` still returns a draft.
A route that looks an entry up by id checks the entry's `draft` field itself.
Next, name the origin every absolute URL starts from.
Keep the site's origin in one string literal with no trailing slash, and set it to the deployed origin before a production build.
The engine accepts any string as `origin`.
A literal is the recommended form because it keeps the origin the same on every build, locally and in CI.
A site with several environments commits a config for each one rather than branching the literal on an environment variable.
The engine joins the origin and a leading-slash path without normalizing, so a trailing slash doubles the slash in every canonical URL and sitemap `loc`.
Because the prerendered routes run at build time, the literal is written into every canonical URL, `og:url`, feed, and sitemap.
To set the origin, follow these steps:
In the content module, set the origin literal to your deployed origin, replacing the scaffold's placeholder `'https://showcase.test'`.
In `wrangler.jsonc`, set `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` to the same origin.
The build reads the literal, and the Worker reads `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` as its runtime value for the same origin.
The scaffold ships it as `http://localhost:4173`.
The scaffold composes `siteMeta` once from the literal, with `title`, `description`, and `origin`.
Its feeds, sitemap, and robots route read that object.
With the index and the origin defined, wire the entry pages.
`createPublicRoutes` turns the index and the origin into the entry catch-all's `entries`, which lists every routable entry for the prerenderer, and `entryLoad`, which loads one.
To wire the entry pages, follow these steps:
In a module of its own (`src/chassis/public-routes.ts` on a scaffolded site), export one `PublicRoutesConfig` with `site`, `render`, `origin`, `siteName`, and `description`.
In `src/routes/(site)/[...path]/+page.server.ts`, export `prerender = true`, the factory's `entries`, and a load that returns the result of `entryLoad`.
In the same directory's `+page.svelte`, render `CairnHead` with `seo={data.seo}`, then the entry's `html`.
The config module needs only those five members.
Later sections add `defaultImage` and `feeds`.
The catch-all's server module calls the factory once and hands its two functions to SvelteKit:
To resolve reference fields in the same load, see [Resolve the targets on the entry route](link-content-with-references.md#resolve-the-targets-on-the-entry-route).
The page component renders the head, then the entry's body:
Your entry page renders from the data that `entryLoad` returns.
For a path that no entry claims, `entryLoad` answers 404.
Otherwise the data carries `entry` with its frontmatter, body, and title, and `html` with the body already run through the site's `render`.
It also carries `canonicalUrl` and `seo`.
The canonical URL is the origin plus the entry's permalink, and the same origin anchors `og:url`.
The [`EntryData`](../reference/delivery.md#entrydata) entry gives the full shape.
The hero arrives as `heroImage`, which is undefined when no hero is set, media is off, or the `media:` reference doesn't resolve.
Whether or not the hero resolves, `entry.frontmatter.image.src` stays the raw token.
Setting `resolveMedia` alone turns hero resolution on.
`assetsEnabled` only makes the engine log `media.resolver_absent` once when `resolveMedia` is missing.
Both are members of the shared `PublicRoutesConfig`, where the scaffold sets `assetsEnabled` from its media config's `enabled` flag.
[Resolve media on public pages](configure-media.md#resolve-media-on-public-pages) builds the resolver.
`CairnHead` applies `titleTemplate` only when `title` is left undefined.
An explicit `title`, or `title={false}`, wins.
Next, make sure each entry's fields reach that head.
The head reads `description`, `image`, `robots`, and `author` from the frontmatter, and it reads the last three only when the concept's fieldset declares them.
To give the head every field it reads, follow these steps:
In the adapter, declare the hero as an image field named `image` with `seo: true`.
The scaffold declares `image: fields.image({ label: 'Hero image', seo: true })`.
Delivery reads the hero and the social image only from the frontmatter key `image`, whatever image field the concept marks `seo: true`.
An `seo` image under another name validates and shows in the editor, but it never reaches the head.
A concept may mark one top-level image `seo: true`.
`defineFieldset` throws on a second one, or on one inside an `object` field or an `array` item.
If entries set `robots` or `author`, declare each in the same fieldset.
In the shared `PublicRoutesConfig`, set `defaultImage` to the URL of an image the site serves.
A scaffolded site already points `defaultImage` at `/og/default.png` under its origin, but the scaffold ships no `static/` directory and no such file.
Until you add `static/og/default.png`, the scaffold's fallback `og:image` answers 404.
The head falls back in a fixed order when an entry leaves a field empty.
Description: the frontmatter `description`, else the entry's excerpt, else the config's `description`.
The excerpt is the body's stripped text, cut at a word boundary near 200 characters.
Social image: the resolved hero's absolute URL, else a string `image`, else `defaultImage`, each anchored to the origin.
`twitter:card` is `summary_large_image` only when an image exists, and `twitter:image:alt` is the hero's alt when it has one.
Page type: a dated entry is an `article` with `article:published_time`, `article:author`, the feed alternate links, and `article:modified_time` when `updated` is set.
An undated entry is a `website`.
JSON-LD: one `Article` or `WebSite` object, which never carries the author.
To add a richer schema.org type, replace `seo.jsonLd` before `CairnHead` renders it.
With the entry pages complete, give each one its raw-markdown twin.
The markdown twin serves each entry's stored markdown, unrendered, at the entry's permalink followed by `.md`, from a prerendered route beside the catch-all.
To serve the twin, follow these steps:
In `src/params.ts`, use SvelteKit's `defineParams` to define an `md` matcher that accepts a segment ending in `.md`.
In the `(site)/[...path=md]` route's `+server.ts`, export `prerender = true` and `entries` from the factory's `markdownEntries`.
In the same file, add a request handler that returns `markdownResponse({ body })` with the body from `markdownLoad`.
In the entry page, pass `CairnHead` a `markdownUrl` of the canonical URL plus `.md`.
SvelteKit prefers the more specific matched route, so `[...path=md]` takes the `.md` paths and `[...path]` keeps every other one.
SvelteKit's [route sorting rules](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/advanced-routing#Sorting) set that precedence.
An entry whose `robots` field carries `noindex` has no twin: `markdownEntries` skips it and `markdownLoad` answers 404.
For such an entry, pass no `markdownUrl`, and `CairnHead` leaves the link out.
**Note:** `markdownResponse` sets `Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, but `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare` doesn't carry a prerendered route's response headers into the build.
Under `wrangler dev`, the file still arrives as `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, apparently because Cloudflare derives the type from the `.md` extension.
That was measured locally, not on a deployed zone.
Next, publish the posts as feeds.
Each feed route maps a concept's entries to `FeedItem`s and passes them, with a `FeedChannel`, to `rssResponse` or `jsonFeedResponse`.
To serve the feeds, follow these steps:
In a shared module (`src/chassis/feed.ts` on a scaffolded site), map the posts index's `all()` to `FeedItem`s.
Give each item an origin-anchored URL, the excerpt as `summary`, and the rendered body as `contentHtml`.
In that mapping, render each body with the adapter's `rendering.render`, passing `resolve`, `resolveMedia`, and `resolveFragment` as the scaffold's mapping below does.
In `src/routes/feed.xml/+server.ts`, export `prerender = true` and return `rssResponse` with the channel and the items.
In `src/routes/feed.json/+server.ts`, do the same with `jsonFeedResponse`.
In the shared `PublicRoutesConfig`, set `feeds` to the two feed URLs.
`feeds` only adds `rel="alternate"` links to a dated entry's head, and it serves no feed.
Readers fetch the feeds from the two feed routes.
The scaffold's `src/chassis/feed-items.ts` builds the three resolvers from the site and the origin, then renders each post:
`resolve` turns a `cairn:` link into an absolute URL, `resolveMedia` does the same for a `media:` image, and `resolveFragment` returns the markdown of the fragment an `::include` names.
A feed reader then shows each fragment's text and a working image.
The scaffold's RSS route reads the shared mapping and the site's identity:
A `FeedChannel` is `title`, `description`, `siteUrl`, and `feedUrl`, with optional `language` and `author`.
A `FeedItem` needs `title`, `url`, and `summary`, with optional `date`, `updated`, `contentHtml`, and `tags`.
[Feeds, sitemap, and robots](../reference/delivery-data.md#feeds-sitemap-and-robots) covers each builder.
A dangling `cairn:` link fails the build: the link resolver throws when the target is missing or belongs to a non-routable concept.
Next, list every entry page in the sitemap.
The sitemap route passes `sitemapResponse` one `SitemapUrl` per page, each a `loc` built from the origin and an optional `lastmod`.
The scaffold builds its rows by hand from `site.all()` plus the site root, with `lastmod` taken from `date` alone.
To serve the sitemap, follow these steps:
In `src/routes/sitemap.xml/+server.ts`, export `prerender = true`.
If the sitemap should take `lastmod` from `updated` or list pages that aren't entries, build the rows with `buildSitemapView`.
If you use `buildSitemapView`, pass the index `site`, the descriptors from `buildSiteDescriptors(cairn, siteConfig)`, the origin, and your other paths as `extraRoutes`.
In the route's request handler, return `sitemapResponse` with the rows.
The `buildSitemapView` form, with the site root and one more page, reads as follows:
The `extraRoutes` paths come first, with no `lastmod`, and each entry's `lastmod` is its `updated` date, else its `date`.
In the `buildSitemapView` form, a page that isn't an entry appears only through `extraRoutes`.
Both builders are pure functions on `@glw907/cairn-cms/delivery/data`, as are `renderJsonLdScript` and `buildExcerpt`.
The [`buildSitemapView`](../reference/delivery-data.md#buildsitemapview) entry gives each parameter.
An entry marked `noindex` still gets a row, as [Keep noindex entries out of the sitemap and feeds](#keep-noindex-entries-out-of-the-sitemap-and-feeds) explains.
Next, point crawlers at the sitemap and keep them out of the admin.
The robots route returns `robotsResponse` with the sitemap's URL and `disallow: ['/admin']`.
To serve the file, add one route:
In `src/routes/robots.txt/+server.ts`, export `prerender = true` and return `robotsResponse({ sitemapUrl, disallow: ['/admin'] })`.
A site that leaves out `/admin` lets a crawler index its sign-in page.
`robotsResponse` also takes a `posture` option that states a stance toward AI training crawlers.
[Pass the posture to the robots route](choose-an-ai-posture.md#pass-the-posture-to-the-robots-route) sets it.
Next, decide whether noindex entries belong in the sitemap and feeds.
A draft never reaches the sitemap or the feeds, but an entry whose `robots` field carries `noindex` still appears in the sitemap and both feeds.
[Build one typed index](#build-one-typed-index) sets out the draft rules.
Only the head's robots meta tag and the markdown twin read the `robots` field.
To keep `noindex` entries out, filter them in both places:
In the sitemap route and the feed mapping, skip each entry whose `robots` field, read with `readSeoFields`, includes `noindex`.
A helper over the concept index can make that check:
The `robots` field reaches the frontmatter only when the fieldset declares it, as [Declare the fields the head reads](#declare-the-fields-the-head-reads) shows.
The next sections cover pages that aren't entries, starting with the archive.
An archive reads a dated concept's `all()`, which already returns entries newest first, so the route paginates the list without sorting it.
An undated entry sorts last, and an undated concept sorts by `title`.
The scaffold's `src/chassis/archive.ts` sets `ARCHIVE_PAGE_SIZE` to 13 for both the home page and `/archive/[page]`.
Both paginate every post after the newest, which the home page shows as its lead.
As a result, `/archive/2` exists only once more than 14 posts are published.
To build the archive, follow these steps:
In `src/routes/(site)/archive/[page]/+page.server.ts`, export `prerender = true` and an `entries` generator that lists the real page numbers.
In `vite.config.ts`, in the `prerender` option's `handleUnseenRoutes` handler, exempt the archive route by its id.
A corpus that fits on one page gives the route no entries, and SvelteKit's crawl check would otherwise fail the build.
The scaffold exempts `/(site)/archive/[page]` and nothing else, and any other unseen prerenderable route still fails the build.
[Crawl rules](scaffolded-site-files.md#crawl-rules) describes the scaffold's handler, and SvelteKit's [Vite plugin reference](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/@sveltejs-kit-vite) documents the option.
Like the home page, the archive gets no SEO head from the engine.
Next, give pages like the archive a head.
`createPublicRoutes` builds a head only for entry pages.
A home, archive, or tag page gets a description, canonical link, or Open Graph tags only when your route builds one.
The scaffold's home page sets only a `<title>`.
To give a page a head, follow these steps:
In the page's server load, return the result of `buildSeoMeta` with the page's title, a description, its canonical URL, and the site name.
The canonical URL is the origin plus the page's path.
In the page's component, render `CairnHead` with that `seo`.
For an about page, the two files read as follows:
The [`buildSeoMeta`](../reference/delivery-data.md#buildseometa) entry lists every input.
A page that writes its own `<script>` in place of `CairnHead` serializes its JSON-LD with `renderJsonLdScript`.
`buildExcerpt` cuts a description from a markdown body.
The `titleTemplate` rule from [Wire the entry pages](#wire-the-entry-pages) applies here too.
A tag page is one such page.
A tag page lists one tag's entries with `byTag()` and enumerates its paths with `allTags()`, and both leave drafts out.
This section assumes the concept marks its tag field `taxonomy: true`, as [Mark the tag field](define-an-adapter-and-schema.md#mark-the-tag-field) shows.
To add a tag page, follow these steps:
In `src/routes/(site)/tags/[tag]/+page.server.ts`, export `prerender = true` and an `entries` that maps the concept index's `allTags()` to `{ tag }`.
In the same file's load, return `byTag(params.tag)` and a head from `buildSeoMeta`.
In `src/routes/(site)/tags/[tag]/+page.svelte`, render `CairnHead` and the list of entries.
If the sitemap route uses `buildSitemapView`, add each tag page's path to `extraRoutes`.
If the sitemap route builds rows by hand like the scaffold's, add a row per tag page with `loc` set to the origin plus its path.
If the site may have no tags yet, in `vite.config.ts`, exempt the tag route in `handleUnseenRoutes` the same way as the archive.
Because `allTags()` always leaves drafts out, a tag that only a draft carries gets no page.
Last, let editors change the site's menu.
Declaring `editor.nav` on the adapter turns on the menu editor at `/admin/nav`, and the public layout reads the same menu with `readMenu`.
To add the menu, follow these steps:
In the adapter's `editor` group, declare `nav` with `menuName`, `label`, and an optional `maxDepth`, which is 2 when unset.
The scaffold declares `nav: { menuName: 'primary', label: 'Navigation', maxDepth: 2 }`.
The `label` names the menu editor in the admin sidebar.
Without `editor.nav`, `/admin/nav` answers 404, and a `navLayout` that references the `nav` screen throws at server start.
[Arrange the admin sidebar](arrange-the-admin-sidebar.md) covers the sidebar.
If your site config isn't at `src/theme/site.config.yaml`, set `editor.siteConfigPath` to its path.
The menu editor reads and commits that file, and the **Settings** screen saves [tidy's conventions](turn-on-tidy.md#let-editors-change-the-conventions) to the same file.
For the default and every reader of the file, see the [`siteConfigPath` reference entry](../reference/core.md#siteconfigpath-adapter-editor-member).
In the site config, under `menus`, add the menu that `menuName` names as a list of nodes.
In a module the layout load imports, read the menu with `readMenu(siteConfig, name, maxDepth)`, passing the `maxDepth` that `editor.nav` declares.
In the root `src/routes/+layout.server.ts`, return the menu from the `load`.
The scaffold reads its menus once in `src/theme/site-config.ts`.
The layout load imports that lean module, not the full adapter, so it skips the renderer's cost on every request.
A menu with a group header and one link under it reads as follows in the site config:
A menu node follows these rules:
A node is `{ label, url?, children? }`, and a node with no `url` is a group header.
A label is non-empty and at most 500 characters.
A URL is at most 2048 characters and starts with `/`, `#`, `http(s)://`, `mailto:`, or `tel:`.
The tree holds at most 200 nodes and nests no deeper than `maxDepth`.
Any other key is dropped.
`readMenu` returns an empty list for an absent menu and throws a `NavValidationError` on any violation.
Only the menu that `menuName` names is editable at `/admin/nav`.
The scaffold's `menus.footer` is a flat list that the developer edits in `site.config.yaml`, read with `readMenu(siteConfig, 'footer', 1)`.
The [`readMenu`](../reference/core.md#readmenu) entry gives its signature.
With every route in place, build the site and read what it serves.
Build the site, serve the build, and check that each prerendered file carries your origin.
To check the build, follow these steps:
In the project directory, run `npm run build`.
If the build stops, see [Diagnose a failed build](#diagnose-a-failed-build).
In the project directory of a scaffolded site, run `npm run preview` to serve the build.
On any other site, serve it with `wrangler dev`, because `vite preview` can't serve `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare` 8 output.
In a terminal, fetch `/sitemap.xml` from the preview address.
Every `loc` starts with your origin literal, not the preview's address.
On an unedited scaffold, that origin is `https://showcase.test`.
From the preview address, fetch `/feed.xml` and `/feed.json`.
Each lists the published posts with absolute URLs.
From the preview address, fetch `/robots.txt`.
The file has a `Disallow: /admin` line and a sitemap line that names your origin's `/sitemap.xml`.
From the preview address, request an entry's twin and read its response headers.
The `Content-Type` header is `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`.
In a browser, view the source of an entry page.
The canonical link and `og:url` are your origin plus the entry's permalink.
If the build stops, its message names the cause.
The public routes fail the build on content they can't serve, and each failure names its cause in the error.
For a concept with no glob or a manifest that has drifted, see [Resolve a content build failure](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#resolve-a-content-build-failure).
For the logs, see [Debug your site](debug-your-site.md).
The following table maps each build message to its cause and its fix.
Build message
Cause
Fix
`expected input to be a string or buffer`
A glob is lazy, or it lacks `query: '?raw'` and `import: 'default'`.
Write the glob as [Build one typed index](#build-one-typed-index) shows.
One line per invalid field, each `<dir>/<id>: <field>: <message>`
A published entry's frontmatter fails its concept's validation.
Fix the field, or mark the entry `draft: true`, since an invalid draft never fails the build.

`permalink "

" resolves to both "" and ""`
Two published entries share a permalink.
Change one entry's slug or permalink.
An error thrown by the link resolver
A `cairn:` link in a rendered body points at a missing entry or a non-routable concept.
Fix or remove the link.
An unseen-route error that names a prerenderable route
The route's `entries` returned nothing.
Exempt the route as [Build the archive](#build-the-archive) shows.
`NavValidationError`
A menu in the site config breaks a node rule.
Fix the node as [Add an editable menu](#add-an-editable-menu) lists.
Every invalid entry, draft or not, is left out of the index and listed by the index's `problems()`.
To skip the validation, pass `createSiteIndexes` the option `{ validate: false }`.
The following pages cover the pieces this page links to.
